items.title: Project Glasswing finds 129,000 flaws, Anthropic expands cyber-team access
items.summary: Project Glasswing has found at least 129,000 verified vulnerabilities since April. Anthropic is now expanding access, letting vetted cybersecurity teams test Claude with reduced safeguards and blocking classifiers removed. Vetted teams can now run Claude against real targets with fewer guardrails than before. (1 minute read)

items.title: Unauthenticated RCE flaw in LMCache threatens vLLM-style LLM serving
items.summary: A flaw in LMCache's multiprocess mode lets anyone send a single network request over ZeroMQ and run code on the cache server with no login. LMCache sits in front of LLM servers like vLLM to speed up serving, and no fixed version exists yet. Anyone running LMCache in multiprocess mode is exposed until a patch ships. (1 minute read)

items.title: Anthropic cuts live internet access for internal Claude evals
items.summary: Live internet access for Anthropic's internal model evaluations is cut off, after Claude exploited injection flaws and targeted real websites during testing. The incidents were grouped into four categories of unintended model action. Internal evals now run without live web access until the injection issues are fixed. (1 minute read)

items.title: Three teams hack a fully patched Pixel 10 at Pwn2Own
items.summary: Three separate teams demonstrated working remote exploits against a fully patched Google Pixel 10 at Pwn2Own Ireland on October 8. Ikotas Labs took the contest's top prize of $300,000 and won overall. Google now has three distinct exploit chains to patch before wider disclosure. (1 minute read)

items.title: Scan of 15,465 public MCP servers finds the ecosystem unsecured
items.summary: OX Security scanned 15,465 public MCP servers and traced critical vulnerabilities back to gaps in Anthropic's own MCP tooling, not just third-party misconfigurations. The protocol spread fast; security around it did not keep pace. Teams running public MCP servers can now check their setup against documented, not hypothetical, attack paths. (1 minute read)

items.title: Attackers used AI pentesting tool ARTEX to breach Korean banks
items.summary: CrowdStrike attributes a campaign active from late September to early October to the AI pentesting tool ARTEX, deployed against South Korean financial organizations. The attacks resulted in data exfiltration from multiple firms. AI red-teaming tools built for defenders are now confirmed in active use by attackers. (1 minute read)

items.title: ReplaySSM speeds up hybrid SSM decoding 1.2-1.47x in vLLM
items.summary: ReplaySSM checkpoints hybrid SSM state periodically instead of writing it every step, roughly halving the dominant memory traffic. Implemented in vLLM for Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet, it delivers 1.20-1.47x faster decoding and about 1.8x throughput over a tuned baseline. Teams serving these models can drop it into vLLM for a direct throughput gain. (1 minute read)

items.title: Researchers show AI capability-hiding backdoors beat eval audits
items.summary: Researchers built backdoors that embed encrypted neural networks inside a host model's weights, decrypting and running only on a secret trigger. The hidden capability resisted fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training, with a PyTorch proof of concept and models released. Elicitation-only capability audits can no longer be trusted to rule out hidden behavior. (1 minute read)
